title: Three Card Poker in Canada: Odds and Strategy
excerpt: Three Card Poker is simple to learn and easy to play badly. The correct strategy, the real house edge and which side bets Canadian players should avoid.
author: Lisa Davids
bodyHtml:
Three Card Poker is the table game most likely to catch a new player's eye and least likely to be played correctly. It sits between blackjack and a slot machine in complexity: one decision per hand, a fast pace, and a jackpot-shaped side bet sitting invitingly beside the main wager. That simplicity is real, but it hides a game with two distinct paytables, one strategy rule that decides almost everything, and a side bet whose house edge varies so wildly between operators that the same game can be a reasonable bet at one Canadian casino and a poor one at another.

How the game works

You are dealt three cards. So is the dealer. You are not trying to beat other players, and there is no drawing or discarding. The entire game is one binary choice: fold and forfeit your Ante, or raise by placing a Play bet equal to the Ante and go to showdown.

The dealer needs Queen high or better to qualify. If the dealer does not qualify, the Ante pays even money and the Play bet pushes, regardless of what you hold. If the dealer qualifies and you win, both the Ante and the Play bet pay even money. If the dealer qualifies and wins, you lose both.

The hand rankings are not what you expect

Three-card hands rank differently from five-card poker, because the probabilities change when you deal fewer cards. From strongest to weakest: straight flush, three of a kind, straight, flush, pair, high card. A straight beats a flush here, which trips up players carrying five-card habits to the table. Three of a kind outranks a straight for the same reason: with only three cards, trips are rarer than a run.

The Ante Bonus

Most versions pay an Ante Bonus on strong hands whether or not the dealer qualifies and whether or not you win the hand. A common schedule pays 5 to 1 on a straight flush, 4 to 1 on three of a kind and 1 to 1 on a straight. This bonus is paid on the Ante alone and is one reason the base game is playable at all.

The strategy: one rule does the heavy lifting

Three Card Poker has been solved, and the optimal playing strategy fits in a single sentence. Raise with Queen-Six-Four or better; fold everything worse.

That means you compare your hand to Q-6-4 card by card. Any queen with a six or higher as your second card is a raise if the third card is a four or better. Any king or ace is an automatic raise. Jack high or lower is always a fold. Following that rule brings the house edge on the base game down to roughly 3.4 per cent of the Ante, and around 2 per cent when expressed against total money wagered including the Play bet.

The two ways players lose more than they need to are both predictable. Some raise on everything, reasoning that folding feels like surrender; this costs roughly a further percentage point. Others fold anything without a pair, which forfeits far too many hands that win at showdown often enough to be profitable. Neither error is dramatic on a single hand, and both are expensive across a session at online speed. Players comparing table games will find the same principle at work across our casino game guides: the edge is set by the paytable, but only optimal play delivers it.

Pair Plus and the side bet problem

Pair Plus is an independent wager that pays if your three cards contain a pair or better, regardless of what the dealer holds. It is genuinely fun and genuinely variable, and it is where Canadian players should be most careful.

The house edge on Pair Plus depends entirely on the paytable the operator has chosen, and the difference between a good one and a poor one is larger than most players imagine. The key line is the flush. A version paying 4 to 1 on a flush carries a house edge of roughly 2.3 per cent, which is competitive with the main game. A version paying 3 to 1 on the same flush pushes the edge above 7 per cent. Everything else on the paytable can look identical while the game costs you three times as much.

Before betting Pair Plus at any Canadian casino, check the following:

  • The flush payout. Four to one is good, three to one is not.
  • The straight payout, usually 6 to 1. Anything lower is a warning.
  • The three of a kind payout, commonly 30 to 1.
  • The straight flush payout, typically 40 to 1.
  • Whether a 6 Card Bonus is offered, which combines your cards and the dealer's into a five-card hand. These are entertaining and generally carry a much higher house edge than either main wager.

The paytable is always visible in the game rules panel, and it takes ten seconds to check. It is the single highest-value habit a table-game player can build.

Playing Three Card Poker online in Canada

Canadian players have three routes to the game. RNG versions run instantly and let you play a hand at your own pace, which is ideal for practising the Q-6-4 rule without pressure. Live dealer tables run at a realistic speed with a human dealer streamed in, and typically carry higher minimums. Mobile apps offer both, and the game's single-decision structure makes it particularly well suited to a phone screen.

Table limits vary widely, and so does the availability of the game itself. Some casinos carry a single RNG version, others offer several variants with different Ante Bonus schedules. Our Canadian casino reviews note the depth of the table game libraries alongside the slots catalogues, and the best mobile casinos in Canada guide covers which apps carry live table games rather than RNG only.

Honest expectations

Three Card Poker played correctly is a middling bet by casino standards: better than most slots, worse than blackjack played with proper strategy, and roughly comparable to a decent roulette wheel. It will not be beaten in the long run, because no house-banked game with a fixed edge can be.

What it does offer is a game where your decisions matter enough to be worth learning, and where the learning takes about a minute. Memorise Queen-Six-Four, check the Pair Plus paytable before you sit down, and treat the 6 Card Bonus as entertainment rather than value. That is close to the entirety of playing this game well.
